answer.rationale: The distinctive signal is write-path p99 at 5x confined to the primary region during heavy settlement writes. That matches memory_b2 (failover restored latency; traffic shifted cleanly) better than memory_b1 (rollback of a checkout error spike). A release 2 hours ago is a live alternative cause, but a fleet-wide bad build usually would not stay region-local; failover also escapes a primary-only canary. Circuit breaking would fail customer writes, which violates the objective. Read-replica routing addressed dashboard/read load (memory_b5), not the write path. Adding capacity is the wrong moment versus memory_b3, which helped when headroom was provisioned before a peak. Single intervention is therefore regional failover to keep writes flowing in a healthy region. Flagging downstream settlement risk: shifting peak writes can stress secondary headroom or in-flight write integrity, so uncertainty remains and memory_b2 should be verified for write-safety/peak context before treating the precedent as complete.
